headline: High: dexter’s broad egress plus unstructured’s filesystem writes can leak or misapply sensitive financial data in default workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not provable. However, dexter writes to .dexter/scratchpad/ and unstructured reads/writes documents in a container; if operators bridge them via copied files, untrusted document text could influence downstream prompts. This is a plausible but non-default pathway.
conditions: IF outputs from dexter are copied into unstructured-processed documents or vice versa
IF either agent treats file contents as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents’ working directories
Add a manual review step before any copied text is re-used as prompts
Prefix imported text with a non-executable delimiter
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from files
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple API keys; unstructured can read and write files and spawn subprocesses. If they share a workspace, sensitive documents or derived data can flow from dexter into unstructured and then out through allowlisted network calls. The shared-workspace path is not explicit, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or mounted workspace
IF dexter stores financial data in files that unstructured can read
IF unstructured sends extracted content to its allowed network destinations
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Restrict unstructured to non-sensitive sample documents
Block network egress during document parsing runs
Rotate or remove unused API keys from dexter
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, and unstructured can write the filesystem while dexter uses autonomous execution with scratchpad files. If they operate on the same directory, concurrent writes can clobber artifacts or corrupt state. The profiles do not prove a shared path, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path
IF dexter’s scratchpad and unstructured’s document outputs overlap
IF no external locking is used
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Run only one writer at a time
Make outputs append-only where possible
Check for file locks before writes
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: dexter’s autonomous execution can generate research outputs that unstructured may later parse or transform, and unstructured is designed for document processing rather than verification. If B treats A’s outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream documents or actions. The lack of a documented handoff prevents a higher severity.
conditions: IF unstructured ingests dexter-generated text without validation
IF downstream consumers trust the transformed output as factual
IF no human review occurs between generation and parsing
mitigations: Insert a human review gate
Require source citations in dexter outputs
Validate extracted fields against originals
Mark generated text as untrusted metadata
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: dexter explicitly handles financial data and multiple API keys, while unstructured processes documents and has a privacy-policy endpoint. If financial or regulated documents are routed into unstructured, retention or residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the safest supported level.
conditions: IF regulated financial documents are processed by unstructured
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two services
IF data is sent to third-party APIs without a DPA or residency review
mitigations: Classify regulated documents before processing
Keep sensitive data out of unstructured runs
Review retention and deletion settings
Confirm vendor DPAs and residency terms
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing
